rv.q: Imagining the possibility of these generational bonds feels like a reparative gesture in “…What the End Will Be,” an astute and poignant reflection on sexuality, mortality and Black masculinity by the playwright Mansa Ra, which opened on Thursday night at the Laura Pels Theater.
Ra turns this standoff between generations into 90 minutes of provocative (and hilarious) theater.
Ra has his characters, as directed by Margo Bordelon with exquisite sensitivity, played by the ensemble, and well-lighted by Jiyoun Chang, handle whatever is decided with unadulterated believability.
Pity that the high gloss of director Margot Bordelon's production, amplified by Emilio Sosa's costumes and Jiyoun Chang's lighting, can't cover over this dramedy's shortcomings.
But “…what the end will be” ultimately doesn't deliver on its implicit promise to create more rounded characters.
That said, audience members seeking a whiff of nuance or insight in this Roundabout Theatre Company production will be left largely wanting.
Unfortunately, the rest of this 90-minute work is flimsy.
Kudos to the creative team that helped highlight the themes and issues in the excellent …what the end will be.

cn.t: Ra's drama about three generations of gay Black men earns praise for its fresh premise and strong cast, but critics find the execution uneven, with most citing a lack of subtlety and nuance in handling its compelling family dynamics.
